interpretations: Count examination records (rows in Examination) per Patient.SEX, joined on ID. Sex groups are M, F, blank ('') and NULL, kept separate. Share is each count divided by the total number of examination rows.
Count distinct examined patients (distinct Examination.ID) per sex group. Share is each count divided by the total number of distinct examined patients.
Count all patients in the Patient table per sex, whether or not they have an examination. Share is of all patients.
Use an inner join, so examination rows with no matching Patient are dropped.
Use a left join from Examination to Patient, so examination rows with no matching patient form a NULL-sex group.
Treat blank ('') and NULL sex as two separate groups.
Treat blank and NULL sex as one combined "unknown" group, which still counts as its own group apart from M and F.
The per-sex average is the total count divided by the number of sex groups, including the blank and missing groups.
The per-sex average is the total count divided by the number of sex groups that actually appear, which may be fewer if no blank or NULL rows exist.
The per-sex average is the mean of the group counts, with M and F only.
The share is a percentage (0–100).
The share is a fraction (0–1).
"Above the per-sex average" means strictly greater than the average count.
"Above the per-sex average" means greater than or equal to the average count.
"Above the per-sex average" is judged on share rather than count, which gives the same groups.
The combined total is the sum of counts across the above-average sexes.
The average share is the mean of the above-average sexes' individual shares.
The average share is the combined total divided by the overall total, which is the sum of shares rather than the mean.
"On average how far above" is the mean of (count − average count) across the above-average sexes, in count units.
"On average how far above" is the mean of (share − average share) across the above-average sexes, in percentage points.
"On average how far above" is the mean relative excess, (count − average) / average, as a percentage.
"On average how far above" is the mean ratio of count to average count.
Output is the per-sex rows (sex, count, share) followed by a separate one-row summary of the above-average sexes.
Output is only the single summary row for the above-average sexes, with no per-sex rows.
Output is one combined result set with per-sex rows and the summary row unioned together.
Time-based or Examination.Diagnosis filtering is applied, such as only patients with a diagnosis or thrombosis.
No filtering is applied: all examination records are included, including those with NULL examination values.

The per-sex average is the median of the group counts instead of the mean.

"How far above" is measured on the combined total, so it is (combined total − average count) rather than the mean of the individual differences.
The average share is computed over all sexes, not just the above-average ones.
"Examined" is based on patients with an examination date that is not NULL, so records with NULL Examination Date are excluded.
"Examined" counts patients who have at least one Laboratory record, rather than Examination records.
The overall total includes only the M, F, blank and NULL sex groups. Any other sex values, such as lowercase or other codes, are grouped as their own sexes.
queries:
SELECT P.SEX AS SEX,
       COUNT(*) AS cnt,
       CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination) AS share
FROM Examination E
LEFT JOIN Patient P ON E.ID = P.ID
GROUP BY P.SEX;
SELECT P.SEX,
       COUNT(DISTINCT E.ID) AS patient_count,
       CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT E.ID) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ID) FROM Examination) AS share
FROM Examination E
JOIN Patient P ON E.ID = P.ID
GROUP BY P.SEX;
SELECT SEX, COUNT(*) AS patient_count, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient) AS share FROM Patient GROUP BY SEX
SELECT P.SEX, COUNT(*) FROM Examination AS E LEFT JOIN Patient AS P ON E.ID = P.ID GROUP BY P.SEX;
SELECT SEX, COUNT(*) FROM Patient GROUP BY SEX;
